items.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995
items.q: The minute you heard Shaw, you knew it was Shaw.

ctx.x: So that after a few measures, people would know who you were. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

Oh. Sound and style. Back in the 30s, the minute you heard Benny Goodman you knew it was Benny. The minute you heard Shaw, you knew it was Shaw. The minute you heard Jimmy Dorsey, same way. It was like everybody had an individual style. Today you don’t have that individuality. I’m not criticizing the modern school of jazz, but I think a lot of it is book knowledge. It’s not you. Now I don’t brag. I’m an improviser. A lot of guys say well Gallodoro’s not a jazz man. No. But I’m a heck of an improviser though. I…
Who were the trombone players whose sound that you might have liked back then?
